description: Strap in! We are THE ZENITH CREW - three Artemis and one Apollo aiming for the highest point in the sky! Presenting Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, an interactive game where YOU become a NASA astronaut. Can YOU conquer Space Fitness, survive harsh Mars conditions, and manage vital oxygen, food & water? Experience how microgravity transforms your body! With immersive animations & super-fun gameplay, we turned training into an epic adventure.

Project Summary: Lunar Rover Crystal Catcher
​What We Developed:
We built Lunar Rover Crystal Catcher, an interactive three-level space survival web game developed using HTML and browser-based web technologies. Players control a moon rover directly in a web browser across three progressive stages—Level 1 (Daytime Training), Level 2 (Lunar Night), and Level 3 (Solar Storm Hard Mode)—assisted by a real-time Astronaut Co-Pilot.
​How It Addresses the Challenge:
Space science and programming concepts often feel abstract or overwhelming for young learners. Our browser game turns lunar resource collection and survival mechanics into hands-on, intuitive play. With simple Left/Right arrow-key controls, live HUD readouts (Score, Shield_Health, Level), and a smart checkpoint restart system that reloads the current stage rather than resetting all progress, players stay engaged without frustration.
​Why It Is Important:
This project combines STEM learning with accessible web development. It builds quick thinking, coordination, and awareness of real lunar hazards like solar radiation storms, while proving that lightweight HTML web apps can run anywhere without complex installations.
details: What does it do or how does it work? Lunar Rover Crystal Catcher is an interactive, three-stage space survival game built using pure HTML and core web technologies that runs directly in a web browser. Players use the Left and Right arrow keys to drive a lunar rover across the Moon's surface, collecting falling energy crystals while avoiding solar hazards across three progressive levels: ​Level 1 (Daytime Training): Players learn the controls in a bright lunar environment by catching slow-falling crystals to reach a target score of 5. ​Level 2 (Lunar Night): The backdrop shifts to a dark lunar night where crystals fall faster and the target score rises to 10. ​Level 3 (Solar Storm Hard Mode): Players must collect 20 crystals while dodging fast-falling red solar flares, where each hit reduces Shield_Health by 33% (allowing three mistakes before Game Over). ​Live HUD telemetry (Score, Shield_Health, Level) tracks mission status, while an on-screen Astronaut Co-Pilot reacts in real time—switching expressions and showing speech prompts to warn of hazards or celebrate milestones. ​What benefits does it have? ​Hands-On Space Science: Grounded in NASA's Space Weather Database (DONKI) and RadLab (OSDR Radiation Dosimetry Database), it turns abstract concepts like solar flares, radiation exposure, and shielding limits into tangible gameplay. ​Zero-Barrier Access: Because it is built purely in HTML for standard browsers, it requires no installations, downloads, or high-end hardware, making it immediately accessible for students and classrooms. ​What is the intended impact of the project? Aligned with CSA's Space Resources for STEM and Youth Organizations, the project aims to spark curiosity in space exploration and web development among young learners—showing them how core coding tools and real space agency data can be combined to build interactive simulations. ​What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? ​Coding Languages & Web Technologies: Pure HTML (HTML5) along with core browser styling and scripting for rendering, collision detection, state tracking, and keyboard controls. ​Scientific & Educational Resources: NASA Open APIs, DONKI (solar flare mechanics), RadLab / OSDR (radiation shielding trade-offs), and CSA STEM Outreach Resources. ​Software & Hardware: Standard code editor, modern web browser, and a standard desktop/laptop with keyboard controls. ​How is your project creative? ​Smart Checkpoint System: Instead of forcing players back to Level 1 after losing on a harder stage, the Restart system checks the active Level variable and restarts only the current stage, preventing frustration while preserving challenge. ​Narrative Telemetry: Rather than displaying static numbers alone, we paired Score and Shield_Health with a reactive Astronaut Co-Pilot who acts as an expressive mission guide, turning basic arcade mechanics into an immersive lunar mission. ​What factors did your team consider? ​Difficulty Pacing & Accessibility: We carefully tuned object falling speeds, hitboxes, and target scores across Levels 1 to 3 so beginners can easily learn the controls before facing high-speed solar storms. ​Scientific Grounding vs. Simplicity: We balanced authentic space weather and radiation shielding concepts from NASA DONKI and RadLab with simple two-key browser controls so the game stays educational yet immediately playable for young audiences.
